claims.statement: The store notes the exact file at its write site, and the commit stages those paths and nothing else. Pinned by the commit-journey unit tests: with an unrelated dirty file AND an unrelated already-staged file in the same tree, the commit carries exactly the journaled journey path, the staged file is still staged for its owner, and the dirty file is untouched. Pinned end-to-end too: the union of paths touched across three CLI gestures is exactly the three journal files.

A journaled path outside the journey directory is dropped, checked rather than assumed: a unit test journals a source file and asserts no commit happens and the file stays untracked, and the end-to-end test asserts no path outside the journey was ever touched. The archive-snapshot boundary is stated in the module doc rather than left accidental. The commit message carries the derived subject alone, so no author or co-author trailer is written.

Fail-open is pinned three ways: a repository that refuses the commit yields a NAMED warning carrying the by-hand recipe, the run does not throw, and the appended event is still on disk; a repository that refuses the add warns by name; a project with no repository at all skips SILENTLY, because nothing is left dirty. Fail-closed is pinned at the writer: a gate-sequence refused append throws BEFORE the append, so the journal stays empty and the log file is byte-identical.

The end-to-end lifecycle test now asserts that the verdict gesture left its own commit behind and that the tracked journey tree is clean immediately after, with NO hand-commit, and that the archive then proceeds without the override flag. The guard is NOT weakened: the same test proves it still refuses by staging a hand-added file under the journey tree, a change the engine did not make, and asserting the named uncommitted refusal. Verified live as well: the four captures each advanced the sha between runs, which is the engine committing its own evidence.

No regression: the full suite is green including the one test that had asserted the old behaviour, which was inverted deliberately with its guard preserved, and the typecheck is clean. The four captured checks all PASS against committed bytes, and the integrity read and the drift read are both clean on the live journey. One architecture invariant caught the new module by name and is now registered with its reason, which is that registry working as designed.

note: DELIVERY (12/20) — the engine commits its own journey writes. Q1 ANSWERED BY THE STATED DEFAULT: the commit fires on EVERY write command, not only on human gestures. The journal is empty for a read and for a refused write, so the common case is a no-op by construction, and a mid-flight agent write is committed rather than left dirty for a person to notice. Q2 ANSWERED BY THE STATED DEFAULT: the message is DERIVED from the gesture in the shape the history already carries. BUILT: an invocation-scoped write journal in the store (the exact file each writer put on disk, keyed by project root) plus a commit step at the surface behind the write dispatch, staged by name from that journal and confined to the journey tree. A THIRD HARD LINE WAS FOUND WHILE TESTING and is now stated in the module doc rather than left accidental: the archive snapshot under .ann/archive is OUTSIDE the journey tree, so the engine does not commit it. It is a deliverable of the session and it blocks no guard anywhere, because both guards that could care exclude it by construction.

RE-RECORDED (12/20). The first conclusion cited only the commit that CHANGED the fix, and the close binds a captured pass to a CITED commit — but the suite ran against the spec commit, which is where the fix first appears as committed CONTENT. Naming both is the honest statement: one is the change, the other is the bytes the run actually read. The AC claims below stand unchanged. NOTE FOR THE DECISION: this gap is a consequence of the fix itself, and it is recorded on the node as an observation — see the latest extended note.

note: OBSERVATION FOR THE CONFIRM DECISION — a consequence of THIS fix, found while recording the conclusion, left unfixed on purpose because the contract does not name it. The close predicate binds a captured pass to a CITED commit and refuses a close whose cited bytes hold a captured FAILURE. Before this fix every capture ran against ONE sha, because the capture left events.jsonl dirty but UNCOMMITTED, so HEAD never moved: the prior node records all four captures against the same delivery commit. After this fix each capture commits its own evidence, so HEAD advances between them and the four captures bind to FOUR different shas, differing only by store records. The pass side still works — cite the commit the first capture ran against. The FAIL side narrows: a failure recorded on the second or later capture is no longer a failure on the FIRST cited commit, so a conclusion citing only the delivery commit can miss a failed run. The bytes differ only by inert store records, which the capture guard itself treats as not an input to the project commands. Recourse if the operator wants it: a follow-up node, since the remedy is an ancestor-plus-path-filter rule in the store, not a line here.
